newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS - MAN sees mild profit rise in 1996-7.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - MAN sees mild profit rise in 1996-7.

text.p: German truck manufacturer and engineering group MAN AG, hoping for an improved economy, said on Wednesday it sees a moderate increase in earnings and sales in the 1996-97 business year ending June 30.
Speaking at the company's annual press conference, MAN chairman Klaus Goette said the company was aiming to boost the company's return on sales to at least 2.5 percent from last year's 1.6 percent.
"If the economic recovery continues, there is a chance that we could see a small increase in sales and profits," he said.
Results so far this year supported his forecast.

Goette said sales from July to September rose to 3.8 billion marks ($2.50 billion) from 3.6 billion marks in the year-ago period while incoming orders edged up to 5.4 billion marks from 5.3 billion marks.

In its 1995/96 business year ending June 30, the group reported sales of 20.27 billion marks, up from 18.60 billion marks a year ago. Group net profit rose to 330 million marks from 272 million marks.
MAN said domestic sales during the first quarter of its fiscal year, fell 15 percent to 1.26 billion marks from 1.47 billion marks in the year-ago period.
But foreign sales jumped 18 percent to 2.57 billion marks from 2.17 billion marks in the 1995 period.
Orders in hand rose to 19.23 billion marks from 17.62 billion marks, while the workforce dropped by 300 to 57,826.

MAN results were restrained by slow business in its truck making unit, MAN Nutzfahrzeuge, which said on October 24 that a difficult European market would lead to a "clear decline" in earings in the 1996-97 business.
In the 1995-96 year, the truck unit, which accounts for about 40 percent of MAN AG's annual revenues, said sales were just under eight billion marks and pre-tax profit was 260 million marks.
MAN's truck unit, like many in the industry, has been hurt by sluggish economic growth, especially in Germany. Sluggish growth means there are fewer goods to be shipped by truck.
MAN's other major unit, printing machine company MAN Rolland, failed to meet its goal and turn a profit to get back into the black.
In afternoon electronic trade, MAN shares were down 6.95 marks at 371.55 marks.
